processing: Fully oxidised Ceylon black tea made in the estate's own factory.
harvest_season: Year-round, as across the hills. Western high-grown teas are generally at their best in the dry months early in the year.
appearance_dry: Dark leaf in the standard Ceylon grades, as is usual for the region.
appearance_liquor: Clear reddish-amber, typical of Dimbula-side teas.
appearance_wet: Coppery-brown pieces or open leaf, by grade.
taste_profile: Few notes exist for this estate alone. Like other western high-grown Ceylon, it should be brisk and clean with a light floral edge.

brewing.notes: Western style. Good black or with a little milk.

vintage_note: Sold by estate and grade through the trade, with no vintage year. As is usual for Ceylon black tea, buy recent production and drink it within a year or two; lots from the early-year dry months tend to be the most sought after in this region.
description:
Kirkoswald is a tea estate in the Dimbulla / Bogawantalawa region of Sri Lanka, with its fields lying roughly between 1,189 and 1,300 m and the factory about midway. Its owners, the Stassen group, describe it as a producer of prize-winning black teas.

It is a coffee estate turned tea estate, like so many in these hills, and it makes black tea in its own factory.

There is little published about how this particular tea tastes. Take it as a western high-grown Ceylon: brisk, clean, a little floral, happy in a teapot at three minutes.

You are most likely to meet it through a merchant selling it as a single estate, so look for the grade and ask about the production date.
history:
The estate began as a 165-acre coffee plantation, named, the story goes, after two pioneer planters called Kirk and Oswald. Accounts of the date differ: one places the founding in the 18th century, which looks too early, and another ties its turn away from coffee to the blight that hit Ceylon from 1869 to 1900.

It was later sold to the Bogawantalawa District Tea Company along with neighbouring Elbedde. After plantation privatisation in 1992 it came under Madulsima Plantations PLC, now part of the Stassen group. The planter Derrick Nugawela held a management post here at one point in his career.
